fix_commit_message:
tftp: propagate expired timer from tftp_state_timeout()

When Curl_timeleft() < 0 we used to return 0, masking the expiry and
skipping the caller’s (timeout_ms < 0) path. Now we set FIN and return
the negative value so tftp_multi_statemach() aborts with
CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT as intended.

Closes #18574
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix ad147ec53de8 on top of intro d3d90ad9c005 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): tftp_state_timeout() in lib/tftp.c is responsible for detecting when the overall TFTP transfer time budget (as computed by Curl_timeleft()) has been exhausted. When it detects expiry (timeout_ms < 0), it marks internal state as timed out (TFTP_ERR_TIMEOUT / TFTP_STATE_FIN) but incorrectly returns the constant 0 rather than propagating the negative timeout value. The caller, tftp_multi_statemach(), relies exclusively on the returned value being negative to decide to abort the transfer with CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT. Because 0 is returned, the abort branch is skipped, effectively masking the detected timeout from the state machine driver and defeating the overall timeout enforcement for TFTP operations. Root cause: A refactor of the TFTP timeout logic (commit d3d90ad9c0) replaced the old wall-clock deadline comparison with a Curl_timeleft()-based negative-value convention, but in the branch that handles an already-expired timer it kept returning the literal 0 (a holdover from the old code's 'return 0' pattern for absolute timeout) instead of returning the negative timeout_ms. The same commit also tightened the caller's guard from '<= 0' to '< 0', which had previously masked this exact bug (0 used to also trigger the abort). The combination silently disables timeout propagation for the expired-timer branch.
